tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Factors Affecting Food Choice

questions.question: Q: Name four categories of factors that influence food choice.
questions.correctAnswer: Social, economic, cultural, religious, ethical, health, psychological, or availability factors (any four).

questions.question: Q: What is the difference between Halal and Haram foods in Islam?
questions.correctAnswer: Halal foods are permitted under Islamic law (e.g. meat slaughtered in the name of Allah). Haram foods are forbidden, including pork, alcohol, and meat not slaughtered according to Halal rules.

questions.question: Q: What is a food desert?
questions.correctAnswer: An area where people have limited access to affordable, fresh, and nutritious food, often because there are few shops or they are difficult to reach.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Factors Affecting Food Choice

questions.question: Q: How does food advertising influence food choice?
questions.correctAnswer: Advertising uses persuasive techniques (attractive images, health claims, celebrity endorsement) to make products appealing, often targeting children and promoting processed or high-sugar foods.

questions.question: Q: Explain what food neophobia is and who it commonly affects.
questions.correctAnswer: Food neophobia is the fear or reluctance to try new foods. It commonly affects young children but can persist into adulthood, limiting dietary variety.

questions.question: Q: Give two examples of how religion influences food choice.
questions.correctAnswer: Islam: Muslims eat only Halal meat and avoid pork and alcohol. Hinduism: Many Hindus avoid beef and some are vegetarian. Judaism: Jewish people follow Kosher laws, not eating pork or shellfish and keeping meat and dairy separate (any two).

questions.question: Q: What are food miles and why do they affect food choice?
questions.correctAnswer: Food miles are the distance food travels from production to consumer. High food miles mean greater carbon emissions, so ethically-minded consumers may choose locally produced food to reduce environmental impact.

questions.question: Q: How do economic factors limit food choice for low-income families?
questions.correctAnswer: Low-income families may be unable to afford fresh produce, rely on cheaper processed foods that are often less nutritious, live in food deserts with limited access to shops, and have less time or equipment for cooking from scratch.

questions.question: Full-Mark Response Discuss how social, economic, and cultural factors influence the food choices people make. (8 marks) <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: Social factors influence food choice through family traditions (e.g. Sunday roast as a family meal), peer pressure (teenagers choosing trendy or convenience foods), and media influence (advertising and social media promoting certain products). Social occasions such as celebrations and festivals also determine what foods are eaten. Economic factors significantly affect choice: people on low incomes may be unable to afford fresh fruit, vegetables, and quality proteins, and instead rely on cheaper processed foods that are often higher in fat, sugar, and salt. Living in a food desert — where affordable fresh food is hard to access — further limits choice. Cooking skills, time, and kitchen equipment also vary with income. Cultural factors shape food choice through established food traditions and staple foods: rice and soy sauce are staples in many Asian cultures, while pasta and olive oil are central to Italian cuisine. Cultural norms also determine flavour preferences, cooking methods, and meal structures. These factors interact: for example, a family from an Asian cultural background on a low income may find traditional ingredients expensive or unavailable locally, forcing them to adapt their diet. Understanding these factors is essential for nutritionists and food policymakers when promoting healthy eating.
